Subject: Recap + next steps: model fit evals (tool calling + structured output)

Alex / Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a short, targeted eval: 

Summary of priorities we heard today:
- Primary: JSON-schema-compliant structured output (order_fulfillment schema) for downstream order processing
- Secondary: Robust function/tool calling with clear retry/idempotency semantics for failed calls
- SLO targets: P95 latency < 150ms for single-item calls; throughput target ~100 reqs/sec for peak window (we can simulate)
- Cost guidance: goal to keep token cost under your current baseline (you shared $0.03/1k tokens as a reference)

What we propose Redwood does next:
1) Run a 1k-prompt fit eval on your provided prompt set (please confirm sample set location or attach). We'll evaluate candidate models for: JSON schema compliance rate, function-calling invocation success, and latency/cost metrics.
2) Deliver a short benchmark report with: per-model schema pass rate, top failure modes (with examples), latency P50/P95, and suggested prompt/temperature tweaks.
3) If we see quality regressions vs. your acceptance thresholds, we'll surface prompt-level counterexamples and suggest fallback model routing policy.

Recommended initial models to test (based on our experience with similar order-fulfillment workloads):
- redwood/volta-13b-quant (balanced quality + cost)
- open/llama-3-8b (good structured-output baseline)
- redwood/streamlite-7b (low-cost, good for caching/prefetch scenarios)

Ask from your side: please share the prompt set + up to 500 representative records and the official JSON schema you want enforced (attach or shared Drive link).

I attached a sample prompt set template (acme_prompt_set_v1.json) and will follow up with a scheduling invite for a short (30 min) sync once we confirm data. Proposed ETA for preliminary results: 3 business days after we have the sample set.

Best —
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2026 18:14:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: model fit evals (tool calling + structured output)

Thanks Marissa — this is great. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Sample size: we can provide ~1k prompts, but please start with a 500-item pilot if that speeds iteration. We'll put the full 1k behind a shared Drive folder.
2) Schema: we have a strict order_fulfillment JSON schema (attached). Key failure modes for us are: missing required fields, wrong data types (e.g., quantity as string), and incorrectly nested items arrays.
3) Function calling / retries: our order API enforces idempotency via client-provided order_id. We want to ensure function calls are retried safely (no duplicate orders) — please include tests that validate idempotency behavior when model returns repeated calls.
4) Models: we were initially leaning toward Llama-3-8b (for baseline) and a quantized 13B for production. Can you comment on the tradeoffs for redwood/volta-13b-quant vs. an off-the-shelf llama-3? Also, throughput on our side will require batching and simultaneous streams; we can share QPS patterns.

I've attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.json (500 items) and sample_records.csv (50 real-like rows).

—Alex
Alex Chen

alex.chen@acme-retail.com

Alex — perfect, thanks for the prompt set. We'll start with the 500-item pilot and scale to 1k once we iterate. Below is the concrete eval plan and suggested acceptance criteria.

Eval plan (500-item pilot):
- Models to run: redwood/volta-13b-quant, open/llama-3-8b, redwood/streamlite-7b
- Metrics: JSON schema pass rate (strict), function call success rate (matches expected function name & arguments schema), idempotency test pass (no duplicate side-effects across 3 retry scenarios), latency P50/P95, per-token cost estimate
- Thresholds (suggested): schema pass >= 95% for production, function-call success >= 98% for critical fields. Idempotency: 0 duplicates in 1k simulated retry attempts (we'll simulate by re-invoking with same order_id).

Artifacts we'll deliver:
- model-benchmark-results.csv (row-per-prompt with parse outcome, errors, latency, tokens)
- top 10 counterexample prompts with suggested prompt fixes
- recommended routing policy (e.g., fallback to streamlite-7b for low-cost routing, volta-13b-quant for critical orders)

We also have an internal eval harness that can validate against a provided JSON Schema (we'll use your order_fulfillment schema). For function-calling tests we'll exercise both explicit function call outputs and structured JSON outputs to measure which is more robust for your schema.

Can you confirm the Drive link or reply with permission so we can pull the full 1k when ready? Once we confirm I'll assign Neha to run the pilot. ETA for a first-pass CSV is 3 business days after we have the Drive data; if that's tight we can prioritize the top 100 edge-case prompts first.

Next steps:
- Alex to confirm Drive access (or reattach full 1k) — ACTION: Alex
- Redwood (Neha) to run pilot on 3 models and share CSV — ACTION: Neha (ETA 3 business days)
- Follow-up sync to review failures and routing recommendation — ACTION: Marissa to schedule

Thanks —
Marissa

Looping in how we'll run the harness/infra for this pilot. TL;DR: we can run the 500 prompts across the three models on Dedicated infra with batching turned off for latency realism and then run a second pass with batching to estimate throughput cost tradeoffs.

Plan details:
- Harness: 500 prompts * 3 models = 1.5k inferences. For parity we'll run 3 repeats per prompt to measure variability (total ~4.5k calls).
- Schema validation: using our JSON-schema validator (strict mode). We'll log parse errors and attach examples.
- Idempotency test: simulate 3 retry scenarios per prompt where the runtime returns a transient network error; verify downstream mock endpoint receives at most one create event using order_id check.
- Retries: Redwood client will use exponential backoff with up to 3 retries; we'll capture when retries lead to duplicate side-effects.
- Logging & artifacts: model-benchmark-results.csv, error-trace.log, and a small sample-level report. We'll upload to the Drive folder and the internal eval page: https://redwood-inference.internal/evals/ACME-42

Neha — can you take owner of the run? I'll provision Dedicated capacity and the quantized Volta image. Estimated infra hours: 4 GPU hours across the run.

-Aditya
